headline: `splitShipments` — monotonic `proposed_at` so back-to-back plans sort newest-first
summary: Single-fix release. `splitShipments.planSplit` calls landing in the same wall-clock millisecond now get strictly-increasing `proposed_at` stamps via a process-local monotonic clock. Without the fix, `splitsForOrder(order_id)` returned the rows in nondeterministic order under burst-write conditions — CI runners hit the collision more reliably than local clocks.

items.title: `splitShipments` — process-local monotonic `_now` so consecutive `planSplit` calls sort deterministically
items.body: Two `planSplit` calls inside the same millisecond shared a `proposed_at` value, and the secondary tiebreaker (UUID v7 id) was scrambled by the intra-ms random suffix. The primitive now bumps `_now()` by 1ms when `Date.now()` returns a stale value, so `splitsForOrder` reliably returns newest-first under any insert burstiness. Same fix pattern as `orderNotes` / `productBulkOps` / `cookieConsent` / `liveChat` / `sms-dispatcher` / others — applies cleanly to any primitive where `Date.now()` precision drives sort order.
